answer: Each identity posts an 80 bond, files one quill-signed, key-bound item at a declared price, and pays a fee starting at 20, rising 2 per 100 submissions. Auditors check price against violet benchmark; deviation over 10% burns 40 and rejects the item. The 1000th fake pays 38 plus 25 input cost, while oversupply ripples the benchmark down 1 per 100 submissions. For 1,000 fakes, an attacker locks 80,000, spends 25,000 on inputs, and pays 29,000 in fees. A benchmark-manipulation ring fails: the median of independent sales excludes clustered fakes. Honest identities pay 20 once and recover 80.
